problem_type: untrusted renderer access to Codex IPC
symptom: The embedded Codex IPC handlers accepted requests from any Electron webContents, including calls that could start login, send director prompts, import skills, or approve a spend elicitation.
direct_cause: The Nomi-H3 Codex IPC module registered nine ipcMain handlers without invoking the repository's shared sender trust guard.
class_root: The fork added a new privileged IPC surface outside the upstream invariant that every renderer-to-main registration authenticates its sender before parsing payloads or causing effects.
affected_population: Users who open any untrusted or compromised renderer content in the Electron process
Projects using the embedded Codex director, skill import, or spend-confirmation bridge
internal_only_reason: The fix applies Nomi's existing Electron sender-authentication boundary and does not change any third-party API or dependency contract.
invariants: Every nomi:codex:* handler calls assertTrustedSender before reading arguments or causing side effects.
Login URL opening, skill import, prompt dispatch, interrupt, and elicitation response cannot be triggered by an untrusted webContents.
The repository-wide IPC sender-binding ratchet remains at its existing baseline or lower.
migration: No persisted data migration. Trusted Nomi renderer calls retain the same channel names and payloads; untrusted senders now fail closed.
residual_risks: The ten legacy unguarded IPC registrations outside this module remain tracked by the existing ratchet baseline and are not expanded by this change.
